purpose: Normative Python behaviors requiring independent Rust implementation, not object-by-object Python interface cloning.

classification.explanation: All Python modules are explicitly classified. Core denotes security-observable behavior, not byte-identical function signatures. Non-core entry points and conformance runners consume core contracts; they do not impose exact Rust CLI, subprocess or fixture parity. New modules require explicit classification.

core_contracts.label: Canonical JSON, request framing, fixed denial/error codes
core_contracts.acceptance: Bidirectional positive/negative canonical wire corpus, status codes and bounds

core_contracts.label: Binding, epochs, registration, signature and expiry decisions
core_contracts.acceptance: Fresh and stale identity vector cases, exact key and subject binding

core_contracts.label: CA issuance, certificate renewal and current peer pinning
core_contracts.acceptance: Without restarting broker/bridge accept renewed cert/JWT, reject prior epoch on both

core_contracts.label: Surrogate authentication, delegation, scope and session budgets
core_contracts.acceptance: Matching authorization, denial, delegation and budget transitions (not convenience CLI)

core_contracts.label: Manifest route, operation and disclosure contracts
core_contracts.acceptance: Identical permitted destination/effect and released subset, denied fields and invalid manifests

core_contracts.label: OAuth vault, rotation, refresh ambiguity and epoch fencing
core_contracts.acceptance: Refreshing an access token changes subsequent egress credentials without restarting, stale epochs refused

core_contracts.label: Durable global revocation across authenticated hosts
core_contracts.acceptance: Registered members stop admitting requests after committed tombstone; offline authority fails closed; restart persistent
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Native account/manifest coordinator client and keyed manifest writes tested against the Python mTLS/SQLite server. No native coordinator server or all-input parity claim; native request fingerprints use the validated native policy document rather than Python normalized policy serialization.

core_contracts.label: Keyed writes: reserve before send and never replay after uncertainty
core_contracts.acceptance: Same principal+key across hosts and restarts at most one provider dispatch; different effect cannot reuse key
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Native account/manifest coordinator client and keyed manifest writes tested against the Python mTLS/SQLite server. No native coordinator server or all-input parity claim; native request fingerprints use the validated native policy document rather than Python normalized policy serialization.

core_contracts.label: Wire idempotency-key syntax and provider forwarding
core_contracts.acceptance: Coordinated write key required, reserved-derived header on declared operations, no caller header injection
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Native account/manifest coordinator client and keyed manifest writes tested against the Python mTLS/SQLite server. No native coordinator server or all-input parity claim; native request fingerprints use the validated native policy document rather than Python normalized policy serialization.

core_contracts.label: Audit ordering, write ambiguity and guest-visible response confinement
core_contracts.acceptance: No completion before accepted effect; failed provider/transport gives outcome_unknown for writes

core_contracts.label: Fail-closed trusted paths, TLS peer pinning, no proxy or redirect
core_contracts.acceptance: Real TLS negative cases, symlink and untrusted root refusal, no bypass of provider network policy

rust_parity_states.implemented-subset: Rust code is present for a reviewed subset; do not claim complete parity without a runnable differential gate.
rust_parity_states.partial: Rust includes related code but does not implement or validate the entire Python behavior.
rust_parity_states.missing: Rust has no matching implementation for this newly required contract.

parity_rule: Every core contract requires equivalent accepted effects, denials, failure codes and observable traces. Exact class/CLI/OS paths and Rust internal data structures need not match.
non_core_examples: python -m aivm_secrets identity command spelling and help text
gh alias and subprocess adapter UI
AIVM provisioning integration and visual/operator dashboards
Python-only conformance runners, developer scripts, diagnostics and fixtures
Built-in provider presets, local session-directory layout and socket filenames
Operator credential-source aliases and environment-variable resolver strings
Serialization fixture generation and Python package import ergonomics
unverified_boundaries: Single trusted SQLite coordinator host; physical hosts have not been deployed and tested.
No anti-rollback for restoring coordinator storage from an older backup.
Revocation prevents checks after commit, not provider effects already authorized in flight.
Provider Idempotency-Key semantics are provider-specific and not inferred from the header.
Only registered coordinator-aware processes participate; mixed-mode/bypassing hosts are excluded.
Python behavior is tested, not formally proved; Rust proof compilation does not prove Python.
